title: Come ti senti oggi?
summary: Emotion vocabulary and a first look at the reflexive verb sentirsi

blocks.title: Sentirsi — come ti senti?
blocks.body: *Sentirsi* is a **reflexive** verb — the action folds back onto the person, like 'to feel oneself.' You'll meet the whole reflexive family properly in a later module; for now, learn these six forms — they're exactly what you need to talk about feelings.
blocks.callout: mi/ti/si/ci/vi/si — the little pronoun that makes a verb reflexive.

pairs.left: *Sono una persona nervosa.* — I'm a nervous person. (in general, essere)
pairs.right: *Mi sento nervoso/a oggi.* — I feel nervous today. (right now, sentirsi)
pairs.note: essere + adjective describes what you're like; sentirsi + adjective describes how you feel in this moment.

lines.nl: Marco si sente nervoso prima del concerto.
lines.en: Marco feels nervous before the concert.

blocks.prompt: Marco has a concert tonight and is pacing around the bookshop. Which is correct?
blocks.explain: Third person singular (lui) takes *si sente* — the reflexive pronoun has to match the person.

blocks.hint: sentirsi, io form + the adjective agreeing with you.
blocks.explain: *Mi sento nervoso* (said by a man) / *mi sento nervosa* (said by a woman) — the adjective agrees with you, the verb form is io.

blocks.speak: Marco si sente nervoso prima del concerto.
